authored_item_inventory.title: Algebraically constructible complexes of analytic field sheaves
authored_item_inventory.statement: Let $X$ be a separated finite-type complex algebraic variety, with its analytic topology, and let $k$ be a field. Let $\operatorname{Sh}_k(X)$ be the category of sheaves of $k$-vector spaces and $k$-linear morphisms. The category $D_c^b(X;k)$ is the full subcategory of $D^b(\operatorname{Sh}_k(X))$ whose cohomology sheaves are locally constant of finite rank on a common finite smooth algebraic stratification with the frontier condition, and vanish outside a finite cohomological interval. These are topological constructible sheaves, not coherent or quasi-coherent sheaves. A groupoid local system is identified with a locally constant sheaf only through the actual local comparison. We use cochains with $H^j(A[m])=H^{j+m}(A)$.
authored_item_inventory.author: /root/klr_constructible_foundations

authored_item_inventory.title: Equivariant constructible derived category of complex varieties
authored_item_inventory.statement: Assume AC. For a separated finite-type complex variety $X$, an algebraic action of a product $G$ of general linear groups, and a field $k$ of characteristic zero, form the analytic action nerve $G^p\times X$. In the abelian category of all simplicial $k$-sheaves on this nerve, take its bounded derived category. The full subcategory $D^b_{G,c}(X;k)$ consists of complexes whose cohomology sheaves are Cartesian under every nerve structure map and whose restrictions to $X$ are algebraically constructible with finite-dimensional stalks. Boundedness is uniform cohomological boundedness in that simplicial category. Morphisms are morphisms in that ambient derived category, not morphisms in the derived category of naive equivariant sheaves. Set $\operatorname{Ext}_G^m(A,B)=\operatorname{Hom}(A,B[m])$ with ordinary cochain shift. Restriction to the degree-zero space $X$ is the forgetful functor. The named construction supplier establishes the derived model, local-smallness and finite-resolution comparisons.
authored_item_inventory.author: /root/klr_constructible_foundations

authored_item_inventory.title: Point operations and the open closed constructible line
authored_item_inventory.statement: Over a field k, the constructible category of a point is the bounded derived category of finite-dimensional k-vector spaces. For the identity map of that point, all four pullback/pushforward operations are the identity; tensor and internal Hom are the usual finite cochain constructions and the dualizing object is k in degree zero. On the analytic algebraic line with j:C*→C and i:{0}→C, the k-linear ordinary localization sequence is $0\to j_!k_{\mathbb C^*}\to k_{\mathbb C}\to i_*k\to0$.
authored_item_inventory.author: /root/klr_constructible_foundations

authored_item_inventory.title: Equivariant Ext of a point is degreewise finite and not total finite
authored_item_inventory.statement: For $G=\mathbb C^*$ acting on a point and any characteristic-zero field k, $\operatorname{Ext}_G^m(k,k)$ is k for nonnegative even m and zero otherwise. Hence it is degreewise finite and its total direct sum is infinite-dimensional. Restriction to the ordinary point is not derived fully faithful.
authored_item_inventory.author: /root/klr_constructible_foundations

authored_item_inventory.title: Incidence cochains of a closed interval
authored_item_inventory.statement:
Stratify the closed interval by its endpoints and open edge. A finite constructible sheaf has vector spaces $V_0,V_1,V_e$ with generization maps $u_0:V_0\to V_e$ and $u_1:V_1\to V_e$. Its actual derived global sections are computed by
$$[V_0\oplus V_1\xrightarrow{u_0-u_1}V_e],$$
in degrees zero and one. Thus a constant sheaf $k$ has cohomology $k$ in degree zero and zero otherwise. Extension by zero of $k$ on the open edge has one copy of $k$ in degree one and zero otherwise.
authored_item_inventory.author: /root/klr_constructible_foundations

authored_item_inventory.title: Actual analytic constructible sheaves admit coherent six operations
authored_item_inventory.statement: Assume AC and characteristic-zero field coefficients. On separated finite-type complex varieties, the actual ordinary analytic sheaf operations restrict to bounded algebraically constructible complexes: $f^*\dashv Rf_*$, $Rf_!\dashv f^!$, tensor/internal-Hom adjunction, coherent composition, localization, base change, projection formula and trace. Proper $f$ satisfies $Rf_!=Rf_*$. Verdier duality is involutive there and exchanges these adjoints. On a smooth complex $d$-fold, $\omega_X=k_X[2d]$, and for a smooth map of relative dimension $d$, $f^!=f^*[2d]$. Coefficient extensions commute with these operations on bounded constructible inputs.
authored_item_inventory.author: /root/klr_constructible_foundations

authored_item_inventory.title: Cartesian simplicial sheaves model actual equivariant derived Hom
authored_item_inventory.statement: The preceding Definition gives a locally small triangulated category with conservative restriction to $X$ and the stated ordinary shift. Actual coinduced simplicial injectives compute derived morphisms. Locally split free-action descent identifies its finite GL Stiefel resolution with the full bounded resolution-triple subcategory on $X_N$. The bounded Hom/image comparisons of the Stiefel supplier hold, including degree-zero ring comparison and retract closure. The normalized functor $A\mapsto A_N[\dim_\mathbb C B_N]$ is perverse exact and conservative. No derived full faithfulness of restriction to $X$ is asserted.
authored_item_inventory.author: /root/klr_constructible_foundations

authored_item_inventory.title: Complex algebraic constructible complexes have finite conical cochain models
authored_item_inventory.statement: For a finite collection of separated finite-type complex varieties, algebraic maps, algebraic supports and bounded finite-rank algebraically constructible complexes, the compatible complex Whitney/conical stratification and deleted-boundary triangulation suppliers give finite local and global cochain models. Ordinary and compactly supported cohomology and ordinary derived Hom are bounded and degreewise finite; internal derived Hom is bounded constructible. Their finite cochain computations commute with every field extension. A noncompact variety is modeled by a finite compactification triangulation with a subcomplex deleted, not asserted to be a finite compact realization.
authored_item_inventory.author: /root/klr_constructible_foundations

authored_item_inventory.title: Analytic field sheaves have injective derived models
authored_item_inventory.statement: Assume AC. For a topological space $X$ and a field $k$, $\operatorname{Sh}_k(X)$ is locally small Grothendieck and has supplied functorial injective embeddings and bounded-below injective replacements. Morphisms of its bounded derived category are computed by these replacements. The full subcategory of bounded algebraically constructible complexes is triangulated whenever a common compatible finite stratification is supplied.
authored_item_inventory.author: /root/klr_constructible_foundations

authored_item_inventory.title: Finite simplicial constructible sheaves have an actual derived incidence model
authored_item_inventory.statement: Assume AC. Let $K$ be a finite simplicial complex, $D$ a subcomplex and $X=|K|\setminus|D|$. Let $P$ be the face poset of its open simplices not in $D$. The exact realization of finite-dimensional covariant $k$-diagrams on $P$ induces a fully faithful functor into $D^b(\operatorname{Sh}_k(X))$, with essential image the complexes having bounded finite-rank locally constant cohomology on each open simplex. Ordinary and compact-support cohomology, ordinary Hom and internal derived Hom have bounded finite cochain models and commute with every coefficient field extension. For a local product projection $\operatorname{pr}:V\times F\to V$ with supplied finite deleted-boundary models, there is a natural local comparison $R\operatorname{pr}_*\operatorname{pr}^*B\simeq B\otimes_k C^*(F;k)$, taking the unit to $B\otimes(k\to C^*(F;k))$. This does not assert that an arbitrary algebraic map is simplicial.
authored_item_inventory.author: /root/klr_constructible_foundations

authored_item_inventory.title: Locally split Cech nerves give actual derived Cartesian sheaf descent
authored_item_inventory.statement: Assume AC. For a strict augmented simplicial space $Z_\bullet\to S$, its category of simplicial analytic $k$-sheaves has explicit coinduced injective resolutions. The derived augmentation is computed by the normalized double complex with first page $R^j q_{p*}F_p$ and alternating face differential. A common internal lower bound makes every total-degree diagonal finite. The same construction works for strict bisimplicial diagrams and is compatible with composition of derived right adjoints to exact inverse image. If $Z_\bullet$ is the Cech nerve of a map $P\to S$ admitting local sections, inverse image gives an equivalence from $D^b(\operatorname{Sh}_k(S))$ to the full derived subcategory with Cartesian cohomology. For algebraic principal GL bundles this restricts to the algebraically constructible subcategories.
authored_item_inventory.author: /root/klr_constructible_foundations

authored_item_inventory.title: Acyclic product fibers stabilize bounded constructible pullback Hom
authored_item_inventory.statement: Assume AC. Let $f:Y\to S$ be a locally trivial bundle in the stated finite constructible local-product setting, with nonempty connected finite-type smooth fiber $F$. Suppose its actual constant-sheaf cohomology is $k$ in degree zero and vanishes in degrees $1,\ldots,r$. For $B\in D_c^{\ge b}(S;k)$ the cone of $B\to Rf_*f^*B$ belongs to $D^{\ge b+r+1}$. For $A\in D_c^{\le a}$, pullback gives an isomorphism $\operatorname{Hom}(A,B[m])\cong\operatorname{Hom}(f^*A,f^*B[m])$ when $m\le b+r-a$. It is fully faithful on $D_c^{[b,a]}$ if $r\ge a-b$. Its image is characterized by the counit $f^*\tau^{\le a}Rf_*C\to C$ being an isomorphism and is closed under direct summands. Extension closure is asserted only for the stronger bound $r\ge a-b+1$.
authored_item_inventory.author: /root/klr_constructible_foundations

authored_item_inventory.title: General linear Stiefel approximations stabilize bounded constructible Hom
authored_item_inventory.statement: Assume AC and let $G=\prod_i\operatorname{GL}_{n_i}(\mathbb C)$ act algebraically on a separated finite-type complex variety $X$. Omit zero-rank factors. Let $U_N=\prod_i\operatorname{Inj}(\mathbb C^{n_i},\mathbb C^{N_i})$, $N_i\ge n_i+1$, and $B_N=\prod_i\operatorname{Gr}(n_i,N_i)$. Put $X_N=(U_N\times X)/G$ and $r_N=2\min_i(N_i-n_i)$. For $A\le a$ and $B\ge b$ in the actual equivariant bounded constructible derived category, the finite-resolution functor gives $\operatorname{Hom}_G(A,B[m])\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{X_N}(Q_N(A),Q_N(B)[m])$ for $m\le b+r_N-a$. On an ordinary cohomological interval of width at most $r_N$ it is fully faithful; its image consists of the resolution triples whose principal-bundle pullbacks come from $X$. The image is closed under retracts. Products of sufficiently acyclic resolutions give coherent comparison equivalences. For the trivial group the identity model has $r_N=\infty$.
authored_item_inventory.author: /root/klr_constructible_foundations

authored_item_inventory.title: Constructible six functors, proper base change and normalized equivariant duality
authored_item_inventory.statement: Assume AC, $k$ of characteristic zero and an algebraic action of a product $G$ of general linear groups on separated finite-type complex varieties. The coherent ordinary six-operation contract holds in $D^b_{G,c}$ for equivariant algebraic maps. For a Cartesian square with $f:X\to Y$, $u:Y'\to Y$, $v:X'\to X$ and $f':X'\to Y'$, the actual exchange $u^*Rf_!\simeq Rf'_!v^*$ and its dual mate $u^!Rf_*\simeq Rf'_*v^!$ obey Cartesian pasting. Proper $f$ has $Rf_!=Rf_*$. Adjunction, projection formula and trace obey their coherent composition identities. The normalized dualizing object restricts to ordinary $\omega_X$; smooth complex $d$-dimensional $X$ has $\omega_X^G=k_X[2d]$. This is not the unnormalized quotient-stack dualizing shift.
authored_item_inventory.author: /root/klr_constructible_foundations

authored_item_inventory.title: Equivariant constructible Ext is degreewise finite and compatible with characteristic zero scalars
authored_item_inventory.statement: Assume AC. Let $G$ be a product of complex general linear groups acting on a separated finite-type complex algebraic variety $X$, and let $k$ have characteristic zero. For bounded algebraically constructible $A,B$ in the actual $D^b_{G,c}(X;k)$, every $\operatorname{Ext}_G^m(A,B)$ is finite-dimensional and vanishes for sufficiently negative m. For every characteristic-zero field extension $k\to K$, the canonical map $\operatorname{Ext}_G^m(A,B)\otimes_kK\to\operatorname{Ext}_G^m(A_K,B_K)$ is an isomorphism, natural and compatible with shifts and Yoneda composition. Extension commutes with coherent six operations, normalized Verdier duality, perverse truncation and intermediate extension on these bounded constructible objects. The total Ext space need not be finite-dimensional; simplicity is not asserted preserved under extension.
authored_item_inventory.author: /root/klr_constructible_foundations

authored_item_inventory.title: Middle perverse t structure glues and has simple intersection complexes
authored_item_inventory.statement: Assume AC and let $k$ be a characteristic-zero field. On complex algebraically constructible derived categories, middle perversity is defined on smooth complex strata $S$ by $H^q(i_S^*A)=0$ for $q>-\dim_\mathbb C S$ and $H^q(i_S^!A)=0$ for $q<-\dim_\mathbb C S$. These inequalities give a bounded t structure, independent of compatible refinement, gluing across algebraic open/closed decompositions. The equivariant structure is detected by restriction to X. Its heart is abelian of finite length; its simples are intermediate extensions $\operatorname{IC}_Z(L)=j_{!*}L[\dim_\mathbb C Z]$ of simple finite-rank local systems on dense smooth opens of irreducible supports, with equivariant data in the equivariant category. If A,B lie in the heart, $\operatorname{Hom}(A,B[m])=0$ for $m<0$. A simple object's endomorphism ring is a division k-algebra, not asserted to equal k.
authored_item_inventory.author: /root/klr_constructible_foundations
